key_insight: An open-weight 27B reasoning model can learn to control real robots through reinforcement learning conducted entirely in simulation, without demonstrations.
problem_solved: Open-weight robot-use agents have lagged behind frontier proprietary models. This work addresses how to train a capable open-weight robot controller without real-world training or demonstration data.
method: Start with an open-weight reasoning model containing 27 billion parameters.
Train robot-use behavior through reinforcement learning entirely in simulation.
Apply the simulation-trained model to real robots for native robot use.
impact: The approach suggests a path toward capable robot-use agents without relying on proprietary models or collecting demonstrations. The provided abstract is truncated, so specific performance results and transfer conditions are unavailable.
visual_elements: Pipeline: 27B reasoning model → simulation-based reinforcement learning → real robot.

paper_title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
paper_authors: Jiaming Tang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Junxian Guo, Fangzhou Zhao, Yilong Zhao
